html:
Thomas Mapfumo is a Zimbabwean musician who created chimurenga music in the 1970s, playing the patterns of the Shona mbira on electric guitars and singing in Shona about the war and the land.

His songs carried coded support for the guerrillas in the Bush War, and the Rhodesian government banned them on radio and held him in detention in 1979. At independence he was a national hero.

Later he turned his songs against Mugabe's government, singing of corruption and failure, and his music was kept off state radio. He moved to the United States in about 2000. He made the mbira tradition known across the world and remains the voice of the chimurenga idea in music for Zimbabwe.
sum: Thomas Mapfumo is a Zimbabwean musician who created chimurenga music in the 1970s, playing the patterns of the Shona mbira on electric guitars and singing in Shona about the war and the land.
